text: Well, here we are again, staring at the ceiling as if it owes us an apology. Remember, gravity isn't personal; it just has a very firm opinion about where wax belongs.
Upward mobility is a noble pursuit for a candle, though I often wonder if the ledges feel a bit crowded. Try not to overthink the ascent; the air is much thinner up there.
It is a curious thing to climb toward the stars when you are essentially a stick of meltable wax. Still, the view is better than the floor, which is mostly just dust.
Take a moment to settle your wick before we begin. The mountain doesn't move, which is quite polite of it, really. It gives you plenty of time to consider your next hop.
Every ledge is a tiny victory over the inevitable pull of the earth. It is a slow dance with verticality, assuming you find stumbling into stone walls to be a form of dancing.
You bring your own light to the party, which is efficient, if a bit lonely. Let’s see if we can find a higher vantage point to observe how very far down the bottom has become.
